JOB APPLICATION TRACKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Know who to follow up with today — and which sources actually reply.

Log each application once. This page tells you which follow-ups are due, flags applications that have gone quiet for a month, and shows your reply rate by source so you can see whether LinkedIn, referrals or company sites deserve the next hour. No account, no sync, no upload — your list lives in this browser and exports to CSV whenever you want it.

Today

Add your first application below, or load the example.

Add an application

Your applications

Company / roleSourceStatusAppliedFollow upActions

Your data is only in this browser. Clearing site data deletes it — export a copy now and then.

Which sources reply

SourceSentRepliedReply rateInterviews

A reply is any move to screen, interview, offer or rejection. Small samples are noisy: this is a hint about where to spend effort, not a measure of your worth or of any employer.

Common questions

Where is my job search data stored?

Only in your browser's local storage on this device. Nothing is uploaded and there is no account. Because of that, clearing site data deletes it, so use Export CSV regularly to keep a copy.

When should I follow up on a job application?

A common rule of thumb is about a week after applying and a few days after an interview. The tracker defaults to those gaps and lets you set any date you prefer; they are conventions, not guarantees about any employer. More in when to follow up on a job application.

Can I move my spreadsheet into it?

Yes. Import a CSV with columns named company, role, source, link, salary, status, applied (YYYY-MM-DD), followUp and notes; column order does not matter and unrecognised columns are ignored. See how this compares to a spreadsheet.

How do I get reminders?

Download the calendar file (.ics) and open it in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook. It contains an all-day event for each pending follow-up. The page itself does not send notifications. Also check your resume's format with the ATS resume checker.

Job application tracker vs. a spreadsheet

If you already keep a spreadsheet and it works, keep it. This page is for when it stops working: the follow-up dates live in your head, and you cannot tell which job board is worth your time.

SpreadsheetThis tracker
SetupBuild columns and formulasOpen the page
Today's follow-upsA formula and a filter you maintainShown at the top, most overdue first
Silent for a monthManualFlagged, you decide whether to close it
Reply rate by sourcePivot tableBuilt in, with sample-size caveat
RemindersYour calendar, by handDownload a .ics with every pending follow-up
Sharing / editing anywhereStrong: cloud sheets sync across devicesWeak: data lives in one browser, export to move it
PrivacyDepends where the sheet livesNever leaves your browser

Moving over

Export the sheet as CSV with headers company, role, source, link, salary, status, applied, followUp, notes (dates as YYYY-MM-DD), then import it. Unknown columns are ignored and duplicates are skipped.

when-to-follow-up-on-a-job-application.h.text:
← Job application tracker

When to follow up on a job application

Most applications get no reply, and it is hard to tell silence from "still reviewing". A simple schedule removes the guesswork: decide the gaps once, write the dates down, and stop re-checking your inbox. These are common conventions, not rules, and no employer is bound by them.

A default schedule you can change
Where you areFollow up afterWhat to send
Applied, no replyabout 7 days (or after the posting's stated review date)Two or three lines to the recruiter or named contact restating interest in the role.
Phone screen done1 day, then 3 days if a next step was promisedA thank-you, then a short check-in on timing.
Interviewed1 day, then a few days past their stated decision dateA thank-you referencing one specific thing discussed, then a polite timing question.
Applied, 30 days silentClose it outMark it ghosted, keep the contact, put the effort elsewhere.

Why track it at all

Once you have more than a handful of applications open, the failure mode is not a bad follow-up; it is no follow-up because nobody remembered the date. A dated list also shows which sources actually answer, which is worth knowing before you spend another week on the one that never does.

Keep it short and optional

A follow-up should be easy to answer in one line and should never pressure. If a company has told you not to contact them, respect that.

Open the free tracker

The tracker applies these gaps by default (7 days after applying, 3 after a screen or interview), lets you set any date, and exports your pending follow-ups as a calendar file. Your list never leaves your browser.
